# Convenience Store: expansion notes (milestones 1-16)

The original game is still the core: the store sim, customers, the shoplifter, hunger and energy, Maya/Leo/Ray,
the gym, Steve's phone and Last Daydream V all work as before. This milestone adds the following on top of it.

## New in this milestone
- **Boot splash:** the Hindu Defense League recruitment poster (Shiva, saffron sunburst) shows before the start
  screen. It is a made-up in-game faction and runs on Game Boy Color only. Code: `src/lw/lw_splash.c`, art:
  `tools/hdl_splash_art.py`.
- **Moonlight Holler Farms in the store:** the right-hand shelves now hold Moonlight Holler produce. It sells for
  +$3, customers never haggle over it ("MH FRESH" / "MH SOLD") and it earns double rep.

This RPG already runs. studio.json lists its sections. src/scenes/town.c is Town, src/shared/ holds the hero, the music, and the palettes every section uses, and src/main.c runs the game flow. Change the art and the melody in tools/make_assets.py. Do not replace the Makefile, tools/gbasset.py, src/probe.c, src/probe.h, src/chrome.c, or src/chrome.h.

It plays on the trusted runtime in src/rt/: the hero is the runtime's player actor and the townsperson an RT_NPC actor, which the runtime draws; the walking is its move.topdown component inside the section's collision, the talking its dialogue component, and the hero comes back to the last checkpoint touched. src/rt/ and src/rt_params.c are trusted too; do not edit them. The forge writes src/rt_params.c from spec.json at every build, so the town is data there: "collision" [{"section": "sec_town", "rows": ["####", "#..#"]}] ('#' solid, one character an 8x8 cell), "objects" [{"id": "obj_inn", "section": "sec_town", "kind": "checkpoint", "x": 4, "y": 6}] (kinds pickup, checkpoint, enemy and npc, at map cells, an npc with its "dialogue"), and "dialogues" [{"id": "dlg_hello", "pages": [["Welcome, traveler.", "The inn is north."]]}] (up to three lines of 18 letters, digits, spaces and ,.- a page). The town's own townsperson says the first dialogue. Tune the components there too, for example "runtime": {"version": "rt-1.1.0", "components": {"move.topdown": {"speed": 2}}}.
docs.cs/work/plan/design.md:
CONVENIENCE STORE. Austin runs his neighborhood shop in a rainy Washington town.

One screen holds the neighborhood: the HUD on top (cash, hunger, energy, fitness, friends; boxes, price,
neighborhood rating and news), Austin's store (WA sign, rainy evergreen window, orange-topped teal counter
with the register, two shelves, the order crate), the striped teal awning, the sidewalk (taco cart, clothes
rack, bench, Maya, Leo, Ray), the blue GYM, the road with a blue pickup, and at the bottom Steve's text box
and the phone.

Controls: d-pad walks; A talks to townsfolk and uses the register (serve, or change the price), shelves
(restock from boxes), the crate (order 4 boxes for $10), the taco cart (eat), the rack (buy a shirt) and the
bench (rest). Walking into the shoplifter catches him. Select moves the phone highlight, B opens it: Text
Steve (a hint), Last Daydream V, Gym, Explore Town.

Gym: A at the bench lifts (energy -2, fitness +2), at the treadmill jogs; B or the door leaves.
Last Daydream V: Up/Down and A pick Fight, Item, Run or Skills; four areas, each a slime then a boss.

# Testing the real ROM

1. Build binjgb (https://github.com/binji/binjgb), then compile the driver against its sources:

       gcc -O2 -I binjgb/src -I binjgb/out tools/rom_test/gbrun.c binjgb/src/memory.c binjgb/src/common.c \
           binjgb/src/joypad.c -o gbrun

2. Run a script: `./gbrun build/game.gb script.txt outdir [save.sav]`. Each script line is one of:
   - `N btns`: hold buttons for N frames (`U D L R A B S` for Start, `E` for Select, `-` for none)
   - `tap X`: press X for 4 frames
   - `shot name`: write `outdir/name.ppm`
   Set GBRUN_WAV=out.wav to record the audio, and use `peek ADDR` (hex) to print a byte of RAM.
3. Jump to a chapter by editing a real save from slot 0:

       python3 tools/rom_test/savedit.py in.sav out.sav chapter=13 card=13 map=14 x=3 y=3 reality=60 flags=4:128

   Then choose Continue on the title screen.

docs.gbkit/README.md:
# gbkit — techniques recovered from Game Boy / SNES ROMs, as GBDK-2020 C

Header-only C99. Fixed-point only (no floats), so it runs at full speed on a Game Boy Color.
Every constant comes from a disassembly that rebuilds byte-identical to the original ROM;
the comments give the ROM bank:address of the routine it was taken from.

| File | What's in it | Source games |
|---|---|---|
| rng.h | DIV-mixed RNG, deterministic 16-bit RNG, weighted table pick | Pokémon Red/Blue, Zelda Oracles |
| rpg_battle.h | damage, variance, crits, STAB/type, stats, exp curves, capture, escape, move-scoring AI | Pokémon Red/Blue |
| motion.h | 32-direction angle movement, top-down jump (Z axis), knockback + hurt flash, SMW run/jump physics, tile-grid stepping | Zelda Oracles, Super Mario World, Pokémon |

Use: `#include "gbkit/motion.h"` in a GBDK project. `test_host.c` checks the math on a PC:

    gcc -std=c99 -Wall test_host.c -o t && ./t

These are re-implementations of the techniques (formulas, constants, behaviour), written fresh in C,
not copies of the original code.

# Goodwill — design notes (from the user's reference images, 2026-11-12)

Flow: title/start menu → job interview → hired at Goodwill → work the jobs (details coming in the user's audio prompt).

## The plaza (ref/plaza_map.png, ref/game_idea_map.png)
Strip-mall parking lot off Prince Royal Dr (Berea, KY area; phone prefix 859-985).
- North row (top of map, left→right): Binmart, daycare, Goodwill's neighbour block. In the idea map: Binmart | daycare | Goodwill.
- South row: Shawn's thrift shop / flea market (285 Prince Royal Dr, red awning) | China buffet (Hong Kong Buffet, "Seafood · Steak · Sushi") | Papa John's (green awning sign, Nails Pro next door).
- Parking lot between: yellow striped rows of spaces, two-way lanes with entry/exit arrows on the east side.
- Real-life look: beige brick strip malls, green metal roof trim, red metal awnings, cracked asphalt, yellow curbs.

## Goodwill store layout (ref/game_idea_map.png, right side)
Outer building (yellow) with the sales floor (blue) inside.
- Back room (top): door to outside top centre, manager desk, clothing compactor, clothing table, wares table, clothing box, wares box, desk, lunch table, fridge + toaster, door into the sales floor.
- Right-hand side corridor/processing: wares table, door (east, near the drive-thru), clothing box, wares box, clothing rack, table, table, clothing bin, clothing rack, door into the sales floor (pink).
- Drive-thru donation drop-off outside the east wall, with a bell for the drive-thru.
- Sales floor rows: wares, toys, furniture, hats, media, baby clothing, clothing racks (several), fitting rooms ×2, two cashier registers, front entrance at the bottom.

## Front of store (ref/goodwill_front.webp)
Long beige storefront, green roof band, blue "g" logo + white "Goodwill" letters, glass
docs.goodwill/PLAN.md:
# Goodwill — build plan (SNES, forked from Super Moonlight Holler engine in /home/claude/goodwill/game)

Build: `cd game && python3 tools/make_all.py && python3 tools/fixbranch.py` (tcc quirks: avoid `a||b` of calls, ternary of
calls, switch statements — use tables/nested ifs). Asm modules kept by fixbranch: engine.asm, spcio.asm (never name a C file
the same as an asm file). Test harness: tools/run_test.py + /tmp/s_head.py style scripts (snes9x libretro, dbg_goto/dbg_x/dbg_y).

## Milestone 1a (first playable)
1. Data (tools/): items.py → thrift goods (clothing, wares, electronics, toys, media, bags, pillows, kids, collectibles)
   with category, base price, quality; maps.py → plaza + Goodwill (backroom, processing, sales floor, drive-thru),
   apartment, buffet, Papa John's, flea market + arcade, Binmart, daycare, Nails Pro, empty storefront;
   sets.py/new art → "plaza" outdoor set, "store" indoor set; villagers.py → staff + plaza people with shift schedules.
2. C: main.c day loop (alarm 7:00, clock-in 8:00 = arrive by 7:30, lunch 12:00-12:30, clock-out 4:30), time clock spot,
   job.c (interview, roles, task minigames), plaza.c (eating, store counters), arcade.c (minigames), home bed save.
3. Sound: store muzak, plaza, home, arcade, buffet, Papa John's songs; register beep, sticker gun, hanger, cart, bell.

## Roles (interview decides; manager can move you later)
donation sorter → clothing sorter (Z rack) → clothing pricer → wares sorter/pricer (stickers, carts) → cashier (register + fitting-room returns).
Staff NPCs: manager, 2 assistant managers, build team (mysterious, other area).

## Later milestones
M1b remaining jobs + performance reviews; M1c arcade (air hockey, Cruisin the Planet Mode 7 racer, claw machine) + flea booths;
M1d friendships/events; M2 day-30 s

docs.hounds/splash/README.txt:
OPENING SPLASH SCREENS
======================
Put your own splash images in this folder (PNG/JPG/BMP/GIF). They play in filename
order when the game powers on (about 3 seconds each, A/B/START skips), before the
fan-project notice and the title screen.

- Any size works: images are scaled to fit 256x224 (the SNES screen) on black.
  For the sharpest result, make them 256x224 or 512x448.
- Each screen is converted automatically to SNES tiles with 6 palettes of 15 colours.
  Bold shapes and limited colours convert best; check build/preview/splashN_snes.png.
- Up to 10 screens. Name them 01_..., 02_... to set the order.
- Delete 01_example.png if you don't want it.
- Rebuild with ./build.sh

TITLE SCREEN
------------
The title art is assets/title/title.png. Replace it and rebuild to change it.
The menu is drawn in the lower-right area, so keep that region fairly dark.

Current splash: 01_anbernic.png (shown once at power-on, then the title screen).
Transparent areas of a splash image become white. Use a solid background colour in your image for anything else.

# ICW toolchain notes
- SDK: BlocksDS at /home/claude/ds/blocksds (symlinked as /opt/blocksds/core); GCC 13.2 arm-none-eabi from apt; upstream picolibc in /opt/picolibc.
- Local SDK patches needed for GCC 13 + upstream picolibc:
  - GCC picolibc.specs: removed the default `-Tpicolibc.ld` (it overrode the BlocksDS linker scripts).
  - sys/crts/ds_arm7_crt0.s and ds_arm9_crt0.s: added a weak `__sync_synchronize_none` stub; dropped the defsym from the dldi specs.
  - libnds arm9/math.c: replaced GCC 14's `__builtin_clzg` with `__builtin_clz`.
- Build: `cd rom && BLOCKSDS=/home/claude/ds/blocksds make`
- Test: `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy python3 tools/dsrun.py rom/icw.nds out.png FRAMES "frame,x,y" ...`
  (py-desmume, headless; saves both screens stacked, taps the touch screen at given frames)

# ICW cast look sheet

All sprites and portraits in ICW use this sheet, so everyone looks the same as in the earlier games.
Characters are drawn from the reference photos in `refs/photos/`. Those photos stay in the repo as references only
and are never put into the ROM.

## From photos

### Rebecca (Moonlight Holler, Goodwill)
- **Skin:** fair, pale.
- **Hair:** dark brown, almost black. Wavy and shoulder length, sometimes worn longer and straight. A side part with
  loose strands across the forehead.
- **Face:** large brown eyes, thick dark eyebrows, full lips.
- **Everyday outfit (the photo):** grey crew-neck tee with a mustard-yellow work apron.
  - Use this for her Goodwill shifts and as her "common woman" ring gear: the apron over a grey tee, with jeans and boots.
- **Farm outfit:** keep the straw hat from Super Moonlight Holler.
- **Change from earlier games:** Super Moonlight Holler drew her with an auburn ponytail. From now on she gets dark
  brown wavy hair. The SML palette (136,72,40) needs updating to about (44,30,26) / (28,20,18).

### Steve (Moonlight Holler co-owner, Rebecca's boyfriend)
Drawn from the man next to Rebecca in `pair_webcam.jpg`:
- Fair skin, big wide grin.
- Mullet: short dark top, sides faded, long brown back.
- A flame tattoo beside his left eye, plus arm tattoos.
- Navy tee, sturdy build. Ring gear: farm work boots and overalls over the tee.
- **Older games:** in Super Moonlight Holler, Rebecca's partner was a placeholder ("sam": tan skin, short dark hair,
  green shirt, cap). Replace it with Steve's real look once that's confirmed.

### Austin (Convenience Store)
- **Background:** Indo-Fijian, from Washington State.
- **Photos:** `austin_portrait.jpg` (an illustrated portrait, used for mood) and `austin_mirror.jpg`.

docs.icw/DESIGN.md:
# International Champions Wrestling: Indie Promotion
Nintendo DS wrestling game + open-world story. Every earlier game is part of the same universe:
Convenience Store, Moonlight Holler, Super Moonlight Holler, Hounds Reloaded and Goodwill.

## 1. Platform
- **Target:** Nintendo DS (`.nds`). Plays on emulators, flashcarts and the Anbernic RG DS Plus.
- **Toolchain:** BlocksDS (open-source DS SDK; reachable over git from here) with libnds.
  - The ring is real DS 3D hardware.
  - The world and menus use the 2D engines.
- **Screens:**
  - Top: gameplay (ring, open world, cutscenes).
  - Bottom (touch): context panel.
    - In the ring: health and stamina, momentum/finisher meter, pin and submission touch minigames, move buttons.
    - In the world: area map, inventory, phone (texts, schedule), relationship list.
    - In the theme maker: the step grid and knobs.
- **Asset rule:** the ROMs we scraped give us data (timings, structures, command sets, design patterns), never their models, music or art. All art and audio is original.

## 2. Modes
1. **Story: Indie Promotion.** Main mode. Requires a created wrestler.
2. **Exhibition.** Singles, tag, triple threat, ladder, cage, hardcore, Rumble-style battle royal.
3. **Create-a-Wrestler.**
   - Body, face, hair, gear and colours.
   - Moveset by slot (strikes, grapples, finisher, signature, taunts).
   - Entrance (pose set, pyro, lighting) and a theme from Create-a-Theme.
4. **Create-a-Theme.** Make your entrance music (section 6).
5. **The Arcade:** the card shop's arcade in story mode (section 7a), plus a free-play menu once a cabinet is found.
6. **Jabroni Hawk Go Skater Pro:** the game on the GameCube on the floor at Joe's house (section 7b).

## 3. Roster
**Sponsors:** Quick Mart and Moonlight Holler Farms banners hang ring

# Moonlight Holler (Game Boy Color)

A cozy farm life-sim: tend crops, keep your guinea pigs and chickens happy, breed new lines, and wander
out to meet the neighbors. Arcade (Dirt Road Brawler 2) and air hockey are waiting in the trailer.

## What is in the game

| Place | How you get there |
|---|---|
| **The farm** | where you start: crops, guinea pig pen, hens, barn, crows, and your farm buddy |
| **The trailer** | the door on the left of the farm. Arcade cabinet, air hockey table, bed, Mamaw Pearl |
| **The village** | the east trail off the farm. Hobbs' General Store, a cottage, a well, notice board, Daisy and Wendell |
| **Hobbs' store** | the door under the STORE sign. Sell crops, buy pig treats and hen feed |
| **Owsley Fork Lake** | the south trail off the farm. A creek with a bridge, a pond and dock, Old Gus |

Title screen: your box art. Day/night, a clock, gold, and a Breeding Book are built in.

### Controls
| Button | Does |
|---|---|
| D-pad | walk |
| A | talk, read signs, use machines, harvest, feed. **Hold A** to spray water (waters crops, shoos crows) |
| SELECT | swap places with your farm buddy (on the farm) |
| START | open the **Breeding Book** (anywhere) |
| START / SELECT | leave air hockey; in Brawler START pauses and SELECT (while paused) leaves |

### Breeding Book
Chickens and guinea pigs each have genes (feather color, barring, silkie feathers, coat type...).
Pick a hen and a rooster (or sow and boar), A on each, and a new animal is born with traits inherited
from both parents. Animals need to be well cared for (3+ hearts), and each kind can breed once per day.
The newest chickens show up in the flock on the farm, in their real feather colors.
SELECT switches between chickens and guinea pigs.

### Little loops
* Sell crops at Hobbs' store

# extras (not part of the build)

`advanced-visuals/` is the pseudo-3D cave raycaster, FMV encoder and display-effects code from the other
version of the project (the one worked on in ChatGPT). Nothing here is compiled into the ROM.

Why it is parked: the raycaster and video code were never built with GBDK or run on a Game Boy, and the
cave scene would need real-hardware profiling (frame rate, VRAM timing). The plan is to get the base game
building and playing on your machine first, then bring this back one piece at a time.
The desktop tests that exist for it still pass on their own:

    gcc -std=c89 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -Iadvanced-visuals advanced-visuals/test_advanced_visuals.c advanced-visuals/advanced_visuals.c -o /tmp/t && /tmp/t
docs.mh/plan/design.md:
# Moonlight Holler — core direction

A Game Boy Color life simulation and small-hobby-farm RPG set around the real Big Hill / Alexander Road setting in Kentucky. Its emotional center is a love letter to Rebecca, who helped originate the idea, and to the everyday life the farm represents.

The design combines the approachable daily rhythm of Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley with top-down exploration, secrets, and consequential dialogue choices inspired by classic Fallout. The player builds a life in the holler through animal care, selective breeding, crops, fishing, exploration, friendships, and choices that change how the community responds.

## Non-negotiable preservation

The original farm is the foundation, not disposable prototype content. Preserve the existing three roaming guinea pigs, three roaming chickens, animal feeding and happiness, 52 crop plots, cucumber / pepper / lettuce / corn / hay, watering, crop growth and harvesting, crop-count and animal-heart HUD, crows stealing crops and player shooing, farm buddy crop care / crow deterrence, day-night clock, living-room environment, and both existing minigames. The Air Hockey and Dirt Road Brawler cabinets should ultimately be accessed inside the explorable trailer interior, not the animal yard.

## Core pillars

1. **Small-farm life simulation:** daily chores, food production, animal care, weather / time, home, and gradual property improvements.
2. **Selective breeding:** individual chickens and guinea pigs have IDs, parents, generations, inheritable traits, and a lineage book. The chicken lines include Ayam Cemani, white-feathered/dark-skinned Cemani-Leghorn-style zombie chickens, Black Silkies, Egyptian Fayoumi, and Barred Rocks.
3. **A living community:** NPC schedules, relationship states, memory of key play
docs.mh/retroable-original/README-from-retroa:
This RPG already runs. studio.json lists its sections. src/scenes/town.c is Town, src/shared/ holds the hero, the music, and the palettes every section uses, and src/main.c runs the game flow. Change the art and the melody in tools/make_assets.py. Do not replace the Makefile, tools/gbasset.py, src/probe.c, src/probe.h, src/chrome.c, or src/chrome.h.

It plays on the trusted runtime in src/rt/: the hero is the runtime's player actor and the townsperson an RT_NPC actor, which the runtime draws; the walking is its move.topdown component inside the section's collision, the talking its dialogue component, and the hero comes back to the last checkpoint touched. src/rt/ and src/rt_params.c are trusted too; do not edit them. The forge writes src/rt_params.c from spec.json at every build, so the town is data there: "collision" [{"section": "sec_town", "rows": ["####", "#..#"]}] ('#' solid, one character an 8x8 cell), "objects" [{"id": "obj_inn", "section": "sec_town", "kind": "checkpoint", "x": 4, "y": 6}] (kinds pickup, checkpoint, enemy and npc, at map cells, an npc with its "dialogue"), and "dialogues" [{"id": "dlg_hello", "pages": [["Welcome, traveler.", "The inn is north."]]}] (up to three lines of 18 letters, digits, spaces and ,.- a page). The town's own townsperson says the first dialogue. Tune the components there too, for example "runtime": {"version": "rt-1.1.0", "components": {"move.topdown": {"speed": 2}}}.
docs.mh/host/README.md:
# Desktop test harness (optional)

This lets the game's real C code run on a normal computer, without GBDK or a Game Boy, so changes can be
tested quickly. `host/mock/` is a stand-in for the GBDK library; `host/emu.py` draws the Game Boy Color
screen from the dumped video memory.

    python3 tools/make_assets.py
    sh host/build.sh                     # builds build/game_host with gcc
    sh host/run.sh NAME FRAMES "KEYS" DUMP_FRAMES [COMMANDS]

* KEYS are held for a number of frames: `R:30 A:2 .:20` (R L U D A B S=start E=select, `.` = nothing)
* COMMANDS teleport and cheat for testing: `100:goto:AREA:TX:TY;130:npc:0:0:0;60:give:KIND:N;50:time:22:0:0`
* output: `build/NAME_f<frame>.png` (screenshot) and `.txt` (game state)

It cannot catch problems that only the real compiler (SDCC) or hardware would show.

docs.README_BUILD.txt:
ROM(s): psx/domino_run.bin/.cue
Platform: PlayStation
Toolchain: PSn00bSDK + CMake (not included); kit files in notareal-kit/psx
Build: cmake -S psxdomino -B build && cmake --build build
Notes: CMakeLists refers to /home/claude/notareal-kit/psx.
Most scripts have /home/claude/... paths written into them; change them to where you unpack this.
See ROM_INDEX.md in the library root for the full list.

Platform: Nintendo 64
